title: In this town, your shadow stays where you were happiest
premise: In a town where nobody's shadow stays under them and each one sits wherever its owner was happiest, I come home for the last week of my dad's crazy golf course and watch the old visitors' shadows slip out under the gate while something wrung like a cloth begins to stand on the last hole's second tee.
twist: The shadow on the last green is mine, from the summers he taught me the course, and the round-headed one at my own feet is his: his happiest place is wherever I am. The second tee was built for a second player, so I step onto it and play the last hole with him.
world: A fenced crazy-golf course in a town park in its closing week: eighteen small greens with painted posts, a white windmill, a pond bridge, a cream kiosk, builders' mesh fences going up every morning, a bench and lamp post by the last green, Dad's brick house across the lawns.
